The manga, which was originally titled Tokyo Metropolitan Curse Technical School, was serialized in Shueisha's magazine Jump Giga from April to July 2017.

The psychology underneath Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is simpler and older than the story on top. After Akutami launched Jujutsu Kaisen in 2018, the series was retitled Jujutsu Kaisen 0—making it a prologue—and released in a single tankōbon volume in December 2018. The series follows Yuta Okkotsu, a young student who becomes a sorcerer and seeks to control the Cursed Spirit of his childhood friend Rika Orimoto.

Behind Jujutsu Kaisen 0 sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Akutami wrote the series without any specific themes in mind, but he wanted to create cool-looking characters. Jujutsu Kaisen 0 received an anime film adaptation by MAPPA, which was directed by Sunghoo Park and premiered in Japan in December 2021.

The nihilist does not deny Jujutsu Kaisen 0 — he only refuses to flatter it. The manga was a commercial success in both Japan and North America. Critical response to the manga was generally positive; several reviewers praised Yuta's role and his relationship with Rika.

What culture calls destiny in Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. Critics found Yuta more compelling than Jujutsu Kaisen's protagonist, Yuji Itadori, who, while having several similarities with Yuta, has a different characterization. Yuta Okkotsu is a timid, 16-year-old, high-school student who is haunted by Rika Orimoto, the Cursed Spirit of his childhood friend who died six years prior; they had promised to get married when they grew up.

In November 2016, Yuta meets Satoru Gojo, a Jujutsu Sorcerer under whose guidance he joins the Tokyo Prefectural Jujutsu High School to learn how to control Rika.

Take away the meaning and Jujutsu Kaisen 0 still functions — that is the disturbing part. There, Yuta meets the sorcerers Panda, Maki Zen'in, and Toge Inumaki, who try exorcising Rika but are easily stopped by her. During a mission, Maki motivates Yuta to fight if he wants to be accepted, which causes him to briefly control Rika to destroy a Cursed Spirit.

The unconscious does not argue with Jujutsu Kaisen 0; it simply acts first. As three months pass, Yuta becomes more skilled, and is able to control Rika and develop a closer relationship with his fellow students. In a mission with Toge, Yuta is spotted by Suguru Geto, a powerful enemy sorcerer who was previously friends with Gojo, and wishes to eliminate all non-sorcerers.

Jujutsu Kaisen 0 feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. Launching an attack on Jujutsu society, Geto invades the school to take Rika by force. Fearing for Yuta's safety, Gojo sends Panda and Toge to the school, where they and Maki clash with Geto, who severely wounds them.

The bleak reading of Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is also the most testable one. Angered, Yuta releases Rika and promises to give her his soul if she helps him defeat their enemy. In the aftermath, Geto has escaped, but is grievously injured and missing an arm.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Jujutsu Kaisen 0. Gojo explains Rika did not curse Yuta; rather, when Rika died, Yuta accidentally cursed her using hidden energy he inherited from the figure Sugawara no Michizane, forcing her to remain by his side. Rika peacefully passes to the afterlife, asking an apologetic Yuta to live a full life.

The self that experiences Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is a committee, not a king. Yuta continues his work as a sorcerer with his friends, still wearing Rika's engagement ring. In 2017, Gege Akutami suffered writer's block in regards to his manga, having lost the motivation he had when reading My Hero Academia and Hinomaru Sumo.

Reproduction explains more of Jujutsu Kaisen 0 than any philosophy dares to admit. Yuta and Rika remained in the same form as in the final product. The concept of the story was creating sorcerers who would be able to stop Yuta and Rika from killing others.

Once you see Jujutsu Kaisen 0 as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Rather than Satoru Gojo, the character meant to recruit Yuta was Maki Zen'in. Yuta's relatives were meant to be included into the story, most notably his sister who would be taken by Rika over jealousy.

Inspired by Masashi Kishimoto's manga series Naruto, Akutami said that Yuta and the Curse of Rika were influenced by the protagonist Naruto Uzumaki, who lives with a nine-tailed demon fox inside his body, and that both would become allies when joining forces.

The cold light on Jujutsu Kaisen 0 leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Similarly to Naruto's story, Yuta makes peace with Rika's curse, which tortures the character throughout the story. Akutami included a line about Michizane Sugawara, a famous figure in Japanese history who is mentioned as Yuta and Gojo's predecessor, as a tribute to a late editor Yamanaka.

Jujutsu Kaisen 0 did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. When Yuta comforts Maki in the third chapter to the point she cries, the new editor Katayama said he liked it too much because he felt Yuta really understood Maki's feelings. Akutami decided to revise this scene in the storyboard following his editor's praise.

The honest version of Jujutsu Kaisen 0 starts by giving up the comforting part. He also said Suguru Geto is a strong villain, believing he could have won his fight against Yuta if he had destroyed the supernatural barrier between Shinjuku and Kyoto. Strip Jujutsu Kaisen 0 of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Akutami's first editor claimed the story was interesting but too dark and persuaded him give it a school setting much to his anger. When learning that the manga would be written in Jump Giga instead of Weekly Shōnen Jump, Akutami was saddened by this decision and kept silent rather than argue over it.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Jujutsu Kaisen 0 shows exactly where that breaks. When Jujutsu Kaisen 0 was being written, the editor criticized the handling of Rika, believing a darker figure would be more suitable for the story, such as Oda Nobunaga.

What looks like free choice in Jujutsu Kaisen 0 is older than choice itself. The concept of Rika was that of an ordinary girl who would come across as evil when being remembered.
